findings: Phone Ctrl-C arrived at telegramFailure as UsageError and was remapped to a generic ConnectionError, so CLI dispatch used exit 1 instead of the cancellation/usage exit.
Code and password prompts can be classified by the provider adapter, so an instanceof UsageError check on the final throw is not enough; local cancellation must be remembered at the prompt wrapper.
Classified flood_wait without a positive safe retry_after fell through to connectivity/retry wording. Duration-specific wording is unchanged when retry_after is a positive safe integer.

deliverables.implementation: packages/cli/src/commands/connect-telegram.ts remembers local interactive sign-in cancellation and maps it to UsageError with fixed wording. flood_wait with a usable positive duration keeps the existing wait Ns message; the same class without a usable duration uses wait-specific wording with no invented count. Unknown exceptions and unreachable errors keep the previous sanitized diagnostics.
deliverables.tests: New helper coverage in packages/cli/test/telegram-signin-diagnostics.test.ts and enrollment coverage in packages/cli/test/telegram-enrollment.test.ts for phone/code/password cancellation, wrapped prompt exceptions, retry_after=120, unspecified wait, and ordinary unreachable. Existing missing-credentials, successful enrollment, cooldown, unknown-prompt sanitization, and transport-cleanup assertions are unchanged.
